# faultline

> faultline is deterministic simulation testing for Go, run by `go test`. A test calls `faultline.Run(t, options, world)`. The world function adds nodes, fault planners, invariants and final checks. faultline runs it once per seed, in virtual time, on a simulated network and disk. Every random choice comes from the seed. A failing seed prints a replay command that reproduces the identical run, and leaves an artifact directory with files such as `report.txt`, `timeline.txt`, `schedule.json` and `trace.jsonl` to debug it. `faultline.RunSeeds(t, options, world, seeds...)`, in faultline v0.1.1 or newer, runs only the listed seeds, which keeps a failing seed as a regression test. For a test that calls `etcdraft.Test`, pin the seed with `etcdraft.TestSeeds` (harness module v0.1.1 or newer), not `RunSeeds`, so the harness's defaults still apply. Code under test runs in one of two modes. In event mode, the default, it is written against faultline's node API: callbacks on one goroutine that start no goroutines and use `w.Net` and the node's volume; every seed replays exactly. In goroutine mode (`Options.Mode = faultline.ModeGoroutine`, faultline v0.2.0 or newer), `w.AddProcess` runs ordinary Go code inside a `testing/synctest` bubble: it may start goroutines and call `time.Sleep`, and it reaches the simulated network through `p.Net` (`shims/netsim`, with `net/http` helpers and gRPC in the `shims/grpcsim` module) and the simulated disk through `p.FS` (`shims/fsx`), never through `net` or `os` directly. A goroutine-mode seed replays on a best-effort basis, unless the test binary is built with `go test -toolexec=faultline-toolexec` after `faultline-toolexec prepare` and `Options.Procs` keeps its default, 1; then it replays exactly, and its replay command carries the same `-toolexec` flag. etcd/raft v3.7.0 runs through the `harness/etcdraft` module. Settings are `FAULTLINE_*` environment variables, not test flags. A test that calls `faultline.Run` or `faultline.RunSeeds` cannot call `t.Parallel` unless it is an event-mode test with `Options.NoCryptoSeed` set. faultline needs Go 1.26 or newer.

## AI coding agents

- [Use faultline with an AI coding agent](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hmdsefi/faultline/main/docs/ai-agents.md): read this first. The loop from a failing seed to a fix and a pinned regression test, which artifact file answers which question, the rules for code inside the simulation in both modes, what faultline cannot do, and a block to paste into `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md`.
- [Claude Code plugin](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hmdsefi/faultline/main/docs/ai-agents.md): when the agent is Claude Code, read the "Claude Code plugin" section of the agent guide. Install it with `/plugin marketplace add hmdsefi/faultline` and `/plugin install faultline@faultline`. It adds a skill with the loop from the agent guide, a `faultline:triage` agent that summarizes an artifact directory, and the `/faultline:replay` and `/faultline:pin` commands.

## Tutorial

- [Get started](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hmdsefi/faultline/main/docs/getting-started.md): a key-value server and its faultline test, built from an empty module. Finds a seed that loses an acknowledged write, replays it, finds the cause in the timeline, fixes the server and pins the seed. Use it as the model for a new simulation test.

## How-to guides

- [Replay a failing seed](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hmdsefi/faultline/main/docs/guides/replay-a-seed.md): when a seed fails. Run the replay command, confirm the trace hash, read the replay warnings, step through a replay in a debugger, and narrow a failure by deleting faults from `schedule.json`.
- [Read a failure artifact](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hmdsefi/faultline/main/docs/guides/read-an-artifact.md): when you debug a failure. What each file of the artifact directory answers, how to read `timeline.txt` backward from the failure, and `jq` queries on `report.json`, `trace.jsonl` and `history.jsonl`.
- [Check that a test is deterministic](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hmdsefi/faultline/main/docs/guides/check-determinism.md): when a report says "determinism failure", or before you trust a new test. How to read the failure, the common causes and their fixes, and the `t.Parallel` setup error.
- [Run faultline in CI](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hmdsefi/faultline/main/docs/guides/ci.md): when you set up CI. Fixed seeds on every pull request, fresh seeds every night with `FAULTLINE_EXPLORE`, artifact upload, one JSON line per seed with `FAULTLINE_RESULTS`, and a GitHub Actions workflow.
- [Test goroutine code](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hmdsefi/faultline/main/docs/guides/goroutine-mode.md): when the code under test starts goroutines, serves `net/http` or gRPC, or writes files. Goroutine mode, `w.AddProcess`, `p.Net` and `p.FS`, `netsim.HTTPClient`, `grpcsim.Listen` and `grpcsim.NewClient`, `fsx.OS` and `fsx.Sim`, crashes and ghosts, the goroutine-mode options, stall and leak reports, and the limits.
- [Replay goroutine code exactly](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hmdsefi/faultline/main/docs/guides/exact-replay.md): when a goroutine-mode seed must replay exactly, or a goroutine-mode determinism failure appears. Installing and preparing `faultline-toolexec`, `go test -toolexec=faultline-toolexec`, `FAULTLINE_EXACT=1`, `Options.Procs`, coverage gaps and `toolexec-gaps.txt`, `FAULTLINE_TOOLEXEC_STD` and `FAULTLINE_TOOLEXEC_DEPS`, what stays nondeterministic, and a CI setup.
- [Test etcd/raft with the harness](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hmdsefi/faultline/main/docs/guides/etcd-raft.md): when the system under test is etcd/raft. `etcdraft.Test`, fault presets and cluster size, scenarios with `etcdraft.Setup`, the checks, the bug switches, and the steps before you report an etcd/raft bug.

## Reference

- [Environment variables](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hmdsefi/faultline/main/docs/reference/environment.md): when you choose seeds, replay a schedule, move the artifact root, keep full traces or collect results in a script. Every `FAULTLINE_*` variable, its values and default, its setup errors and log lines, and how it combines with `Options`.
- [Artifact files](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hmdsefi/faultline/main/docs/reference/artifacts.md): when a script reads an artifact, or you need the exact meaning of a field. The artifact directory path, and the format and fields of `report.json`, `report.txt`, `trace.jsonl` and its record kinds, `timeline.txt`, `schedule.json`, `history.jsonl`, `hb.mmd` and `timeline.html`.
- [The faultline-toolexec command](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hmdsefi/faultline/main/docs/reference/toolexec.md): when you set up or debug exact replay. Install, `prepare`, the state directory, the `FAULTLINE_TOOLEXEC_*` variables, the rewrite set, what a rewrite changes, every coverage gap kind, and the error messages.
- [The faultline command](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hmdsefi/faultline/main/docs/reference/cli.md): when you need a larger causal slice, or the rendered files of an artifact from CI. `faultline render` and `faultline version`, their flags, output and exit codes.
- [Package faultline on pkg.go.dev](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/hmdsefi/faultline): when you need a signature or the default of an option. `Run`, `RunSeeds`, `Options`, `World` and `Process`, and the packages `kernel`, `kernel/simnet`, `kernel/simdisk`, `kernel/fault` and `check/history`, with runnable examples, and `shims/netsim` and `shims/fsx`.
- [Package grpcsim on pkg.go.dev](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/hmdsefi/faultline/shims/grpcsim): when a process serves or calls gRPC. `Listen`, `NewClient`, `Target` and `WithHost`.
- [Package etcdraft on pkg.go.dev](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/hmdsefi/faultline/harness/etcdraft): when you configure the etcd/raft harness. Every `Config` field and `Cluster` method of the etcd/raft harness.

## Concepts

- [How faultline works](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hmdsefi/faultline/main/docs/how-it-works.md): when you write code that runs inside the simulation, or need to know why a run behaves as it does. Virtual time, the seeded scheduler, named random streams, nodes, the simulated network and disk, goroutine mode, faults and fault schedules, checks, seeds and replay, and the determinism rules for code under test in each mode.
- [Architecture](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hmdsefi/faultline/main/docs/architecture.md): when you need to know what the node API is or which package does what. The node API and goroutine mode, the packages and modules, how one seed runs through them, and the design choices behind them, including the toolexec backend.
- [Limitations and FAQ](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hmdsefi/faultline/main/docs/faq.md): before you decide whether faultline fits a system, when a feature seems to be missing, or when `go get` of a nested module fails with "does not contain package". What faultline does not do, the known issues, how to add a nested module at a specific version, and how faultline relates to FoundationDB's simulation testing, TigerBeetle's VOPR, Antithesis, Jepsen and `testing/synctest`.

## Optional

- [README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hmdsefi/faultline/main/README.md): overview, install commands and status.
- [Contributing](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hmdsefi/faultline/main/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md): when you change faultline itself. Build and test commands, and the determinism rules for faultline's own packages.
